subject: Usage variability stabilization & GPU hedge proposal
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martín <elena@cobalttherapeutics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Usage variability stabilization & GPU hedge proposal

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call today. Cobalt's burst-to-steady usage pattern is clear from the April telemetry you shared; we saw short, high-concurrency windows followed by long idle tails. I put together an operational approach that aims to: reduce thermal/queue risk during spikes, avoid overcommitting reserved tranches, and give you predictable unit economics for the coming 12 months.

High level proposal (attached):
- 6-month staged hedge: +12 H100-equivalent slots reserved as a tolerated buffer for Q3 spikes, released gradually if monthly peak variance stays below 18%.
- Smoothing policy: auto-burst credits (consumable at 2x standard throughput) for up to 10 events/month with per-event caps tied to historical 99th percentile.
- Observability & rollback: per-model token latency SLOs, plus an automated warm fallback to quantized model variant when thermal headroom is low.

Attachments: cobalt_usage_apr2025.csv (usage samples), gpu_hedge_proposal_v1.xlsx (numbers), sla-88ms-latency-draft.pdf (SLA sketch).

As next steps, if this direction looks reasonable I can route a formal SOW and a short mutual action plan for signature. Curious what procurement will need on timing and whether a 6-month pilot with opt-in topup makes sense.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0126

From: Elena Martín <elena@cobalttherapeutics.com>

Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage variability stabilization & GPU hedge proposal

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clarity. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

1) Procurement asked whether we can convert the hedge into a committed tranching credit if utilization stabilizes sooner — i.e. credits convert to discounted committed slots after 90 days if utilization > 75% on average.
2) Our infra team needs a short runbook that spells out how the auto-burst credits are consumed and what notification cadence they get when fallback to quantized model occurs. We also want the ability to opt out of auto-quantize on a per-model basis.
3) SLA: the 88ms draft looks reasonable but can you confirm what latency percentile that's measured over (p95/p99) and whether it applies to the quantized fallback variant.

We'd like to move quickly; is there a 30-page procurement checklist you typically supply? If not, point me to the minimum items and we can start redlining.

Best,
Elena Martín
Head of Platform, Cobalt Therapeutics
elena@cobalttherapeutics.com

Team —

Quick read on numbers and options for procurement:
- Baseline: Cobalt current committed runrate = 120 H100-eq hours/day average. April peak 18x baseline for 2 short windows (6–12 minutes).
- Hedge ask: +12 reserved slots yields ~20% headroom on sustained concurrency, and reduces queued requests during peaks by ~65% in our sim.
- Costing options: (A) Short-term buffer: $X/month per slot (billed as reserved credit, refundable after 6 months if unused). (B) Convertible credit: 90-day conditional conversion to committed slots at 12% discount if utilization threshold hit.

Engineering notes to include in runbook (Mina): please add explicit triggers for auto-burst consumption, notification templates, and steps to opt-out of quantized fallback. Marissa: can you produce the conversion math and a 12-month cashflow table for both options A and B by EOD?

Olga — once we have the conversion matrix and runbook excerpts I'll draft the minimal procurement checklist (SOC2 attestation snippet, data retention policy, export controls, per-route latency SLOs, and the billing appendix).

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martín <elena@cobalttherapeutics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Usage variability stabilization & GPU hedge proposal

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the questions. Attached is a thinner packet for procurement (minimal checklist + conversion matrix) and an excerpted runbook that shows the exact burst-consumption path and the opt-out flow for quantized fallbacks. Highlights below: 

- Conversion mechanics: after a 90-day observation window, if average utilization across the leased tranche >= 75% we will convert consumed credits into committed slots at a 12% discount vs standard committed pricing. Conversion is one-way and triggers on the 91st day.
- Burst consumption: auto-burst uses credits from the reserved hedge pool first; when credits drop below a 20% cushion we send an automated alert to the Cobalt on-call email and open a transient incident in the Redwood Console.
- SLA metrics: latency targets are measured at p95 for the primary model variant and p99 for the quantized fallback (we include an elevated margin for quantized throughput). See sla-88ms-latency-draft.pdf for the exact language.
- Pricing table and a 12-month cashflow projection are attached (gpu_hedge_proposal_v1.xlsx). Marissa included two scenarios (conservative and aggressive).

If this aligns, procurement can execute a short MSA addendum and a 6-month hedge SOW. I'll schedule a 30-minute sign-off call next week with procurement + infra to walk the runbook and conversion table. Available slots: Tue 13th 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 14th 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Attachments: minimal_procurement_checklist.pdf (procurement essentials), gpu_hedge_proposal_v1.xlsx, runbook_excerpts.txt
thread_summary: Customer (Cobalt) experiences short high-concurrency spikes. Proposal: 6-month hedge of reserved GPU slots (+12 H100-eq) with auto-burst credits and a 90-day convertible clause to turn credits into committed slots at discount if utilization stabilizes. Internal coordination produced a conversion matrix, runbook excerpt, and procurement checklist. Customer requested clarification on SLA percentiles and opt-out of quantized fallback; those items were addressed and a sign-off call scheduled.
